events.title: Big catering order
events.description: A company wants catering for 200 people next month. You must buy ingredients and hire extra staff now — they pay 60 days after the event.

yes.label: Take the order
yes.explanation: Profitable, but you pay costs today and get money in two months. Without a reserve this can drain your cash.

no.label: Decline
no.explanation: You keep your cash safe, but miss a profitable client who might have come back.

events.concept: Payment terms and cash flow gap

events.title: Fridge breaks down
events.description: Your main fridge died on a Friday. A repair costs 6,000 now; a new energy-efficient one costs 15,000 but cuts electricity bills.

yes.label: Buy a new one
yes.explanation: Higher cost today, lower costs every month after. It pays back in about 2 years.

no.label: Just repair it
no.explanation: Cheaper now, but the old fridge keeps using more energy and may break again.

events.title: Quiet winter season
events.description: Foot traffic drops for the next months. A marketing agency offers a winter campaign for 5,000.

yes.label: Run the campaign
yes.explanation: Marketing can soften a seasonal dip, but results are never guaranteed.

no.label: Wait it out
no.explanation: You save cash, but revenue falls. This is exactly when a reserve helps.

events.title: Bulk stock discount
events.description: Your supplier offers 25% off if you buy 6 months of stock upfront for 30,000.

yes.label: Buy in bulk
yes.explanation: Lower unit costs later, but a big chunk of cash is now frozen in your warehouse.

no.label: Keep buying monthly
no.explanation: You pay more per item, but your cash stays flexible for surprises.

events.title: Ad platform price hike
events.description: Your main ad channel raised prices by 40%. You can keep spending or move budget to email and SEO, which takes months to work.

yes.label: Keep paying for ads
yes.explanation: Sales stay stable, but your margin shrinks every month.

no.label: Switch to SEO & email
no.explanation: A short-term dip for a cheaper, more independent sales channel later.

events.title: Wave of returns
events.description: A faulty batch from your supplier leads to many returns. You can refund everyone immediately or argue case by case.

yes.label: Refund everyone now
yes.explanation: It hurts today, but protects your reviews — your most valuable long-term asset.

no.label: Handle case by case
no.explanation: You save money now, but bad reviews quietly lower sales for months.

events.title: One giant client
events.description: A corporation offers a contract worth 60% of your revenue. They want you to drop smaller clients to focus on them.

yes.label: Sign the contract
yes.explanation: More revenue, but if this one client leaves, you lose most of your income at once.

no.label: Stay diversified
no.explanation: Slower growth, but no single client can sink your company.

events.title: Invoice 60 days late
events.description: Your biggest client delays a 20,000 payment by two months. A factoring company offers the cash now for a 3% fee.

yes.label: Use factoring
yes.explanation: You pay a small fee to keep cash flowing. Worth it only when you have no reserve.

no.label: Wait for payment
no.explanation: Free, but the missing 20,000 has to come from your cash or reserve meanwhile.

events.title: Hire a senior developer
events.description: A great senior developer is available. They cost 15,000 per month, but would let you take on bigger projects.

yes.label: Hire
yes.explanation: Fixed costs rise immediately, while extra revenue depends on winning new projects.

no.label: Not now
no.explanation: Lower risk, but you may turn down larger projects.

events.title: Market drops 15%
events.description: Stock markets fell 15% this month. Headlines are scary. Do you sell your ETF to stop the loss?

yes.label: Sell everything
yes.explanation: Selling locks in the loss. Historically, broad markets recovered — but only for those who stayed invested.

no.label: Hold
no.explanation: Your portfolio is down on paper. With a long horizon, holding gives it time to recover.
